item.title: Realization of several related $(2+1)$-dimensional integrable systems via an anti-self-dual Yang--Mills reduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.22753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive several integrable equations in $(2+1)$ dimensions from the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills (ASDYM) equations with gauge group $G=\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb C)$ by imposing a single one-dimensional constraint on the ASDYM matrices. The resulting systems include the $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equation, a $(2+1)$-dimensional generalized derivative NLS family encompassing the Gerdjikov--Ivanov, Chen--Lee--Liu, and Kaup--Newell equations, and the $(2+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnetic (HF) equation. The $(1+1)$-dimensional Wadati--Konno--Ichikawa equation is also recovered through a reciprocal transformation of the HF equation. The nonlinear variables and the associated gauge transformations are expressed explicitly in terms of the entries of the ASDYM matrices. The same one-dimensional constraint is implemented in the Cauchy matrix framework, yielding explicit solutions of the reduced integrable equations. In this formulation, the ASD Yang--Mills Lagrangian density is expressed in terms of a $\tau$-function; for suitable exponential data, this $\tau$-function becomes a Grammian-type $\tau$-function of the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili equaton. The studies are extended to $\mathrm{GL}(M,\mathbb C)$ at the matrix level.
item.dc:creator: Shangshuai Li, Ken-ichi Maruno, Da-jun Zhang

item.title: Hyperelliptic sigma solutions of polynomial Hamiltonian systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.22784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study polynomial Hamiltonian systems whose Hamiltonians consist of two weighted products of canonical modes minus a polynomial in their powers. This class extends the structure of familiar genus-one coupled-mode systems from nonlinear optics. We construct local analytic solutions in terms of sigma functions and Abelian integrals on smooth odd-degree hyperelliptic curves, subject to stated degree and regularity conditions. We associate Onishi's determinant identities with the conservation-law structure of these systems, extending the connection previously identified between Frobenius-Stickelberger determinants and conserved quantities in genus-one nonlinear optics. Explicit genus-two and genus-three examples include bounded oscillatory scalar motion. We evaluate the solutions using Generapy, a purpose-built Python package for algebraic curves and Abelian functions, and validate them against independent fourth-order Runge-Kutta integration.
item.dc:creator: Graham Hesketh

item.title: Folding to the Bessel-Clifford system, and Equivariant Topological Recursion
item.description: arXiv:2610.23320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the interplay between symmetry reductions of meromorphic connections, folding, and topological recursion. As a motivating example, we realize the Bessel-Clifford system as a folding of a symmetry-invariant subspace of the $0-$member of the Painlev\'e IV hierarchy. We introduce equivariant topological recursion for spectral curves with a Klein four-group $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry and prove that the corresponding equivariant correlators can be folded to the ordinary topological recursion correlators on the quotient spectral curve. We further establish the compatibility of this folding with the associated wave functions and quantum curves. In the Bessel-Clifford example, this yields an explicit relation between the equivariant and folded wave functions and recovers the corresponding quantum curve reduction. These results provide a framework for relating symmetry reductions of integrable systems to folding operations in topological recursion.
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Alameddine, Alexander Hock

item.title: A generalized long-wave limit method with spectral perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2606.15174v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a generalized long-wave limit method for constructing higher-order (degenerate) lump solutions of $(2+1)$-dimensional integrable systems. Starting from the multi-soliton tau function, we introduce wavenumber rescalings, spectral perturbations, and higher-order phase modulations in a single small parameter, and choose their coefficients so that the lower-order Taylor coefficients vanish. Applying this framework to the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili I equation, we explicitly derive second-order two- and three-lump solutions as well as third-order three-, four-, five-, and six-lump solutions. The long-time asymptotics of the peak positions and amplitudes describe anomalous scattering of these degenerate lump solutions. Extensions to hybrid higher-order lump solutions associated with multiple distinct spectral parameters are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang

item.title: Rogue-like waves from collision of mKdV solitons
item.description: arXiv:2609.10512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Interactions of two solitary waves having an up and a down orientation in the modified Korteweg-de Vries equation are shown to produce rogue-like waves. For waves that asymptotically vanish, the maximum ratio between the net peak-to-trough height of the interaction profile and the height of the tallest incoming wave is 2.41 when the waves have approximately equal speeds, and this ratio decreases to 2 when the speed ratio is 2.25. For waves that approach a non-zero constant at infinity, the same ratio is always greater than 2.41 and reaches a maximum of 2.65 when the speed ratio of the waves is 6.32.
item.dc:creator: Stephen C. Anco, Jaskaran Maan

item.title: Exact Chained-Word Threshold and Monotone-Path Structure in the Even Root-of-Unity Kaleidoscope Yang-Baxter Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2609.39262v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Qiu, Guan, and Yu conjectured that in the even-order Kaleidoscope Yang--Baxter equation every word $\Lambda T^{k_1}\Lambda\cdots T^{k_M}\Lambda$, built from a square-zero matrix $\Lambda$ and integer powers of a shift $T$ of order $N$, vanishes once $M\geq N/2$. We prove this for every even $N\geq4$ and every complex parameter $u$ with $u\neq0$ and $u^N\neq1$, and show that the bound is sharp. For $M=N/2-1$ we determine exactly which words are nonzero; each of them has rank two. After block reduction, the factors associated with the intervening powers of $T$ lower a common flag of length $N/2$ by at least one step. The spectral idempotents of $T$ then give a presentation of the algebra generated by $T$ and $\Lambda$ by paths between levels, in which two paths compose only when the level changes monotonically. This algebra is independent of $u$, has dimension $N^2-N+2$, and is a pullback of two incidence algebras. Its radical is generated by $\Lambda$ and has nilpotency index $N/2+1$, and the algebra has infinite global dimension and infinite representation type. Replacing powers of $T$ by arbitrary functions of $T$ gives exact rank formulas and, for $N\geq6$, rank-one elements in the top radical power. Finally, four conditions on a filtered pair of operators over an arbitrary field recover the threshold and the radical; none of them can be omitted.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang, Zhiyuan Yao
